findings.evidenceJa: ずるり、と滑る腕で地面を掴み
findings.governingReading: He grips the ground with his arm slipping slickly beneath him.
findings.explanation: The English omits the unstable sliding of the only limb supporting his nearly severed body.

findings.governingReading: the faint beat of his heart
findings.explanation: The English removes the faintness that marks Shirou as barely alive.

findings.evidenceJa: ギチギチと音をたてる、傷ついた内臓
findings.governingReading: his damaged internal organs making a tight creaking or grinding sound
findings.explanation: The English invents personified pain and omits that the injured organs produce the same mechanical sound later associated with internal blades.

findings.highlight: With a creaking noise, my body reacts
findings.evidenceJa: 体は鈍い音をたてながら
findings.governingReading: His body answers his will while making a dull, heavy sound.
findings.explanation: Creaking supplies a different acoustic quality from the source’s muffled, dull impact-like noise.

findings.highlight: the things I need to live flow out
findings.evidenceJa: 生きていくのに必要なものがごっそりとこぼれ落ちていく
findings.governingReading: something necessary for life spills out of the wound in a great mass each time he strains
findings.explanation: The English loses the wholesale quantity and changes spilling from a wound into neutral flowing.

findings.evidenceJa: 俺のあがきを嘲笑っているギルガメッシュ
findings.governingReading: Gilgamesh, who is laughing Shirou’s desperate struggle to scorn
findings.explanation: The English lists Gilgamesh as an obstacle but removes his active mockery of Shirou’s effort.

findings.evidenceJa: この心が折れて、しまう
findings.governingReading: his heart or resolve will break
findings.explanation: Mind will die is nonidiomatic and turns emotional collapse into cognitive death.

findings.evidenceJa: こんな事で貴方に死なれたら
findings.governingReading: If Shirou dies over something like this or for this cause
findings.explanation: Here converts Saber’s anguished judgment of cause and worth into physical location.

findings.highlight: So that you can be proud of your life
findings.evidenceJa: 胸を張って眠れるように
findings.governingReading: so that at death Saber can hold her head high and go to sleep, proud of her life
findings.explanation: The English retains pride but omits sleep, the merciful completion of Shirou’s wish for Saber’s final rest.

findings.highlight: I can’t give Saber to you.
findings.evidenceJa: おまえに、セイバーは任せられない
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot entrust Saber to Gilgamesh.
findings.explanation: Give Saber to you repeats the ownership framing Shirou has just rejected; 任せる concerns trust and care, not transfer of property.

findings.highlight: the light that can burn away everything it touches
findings.evidenceJa: 触れるモノを焼き払う光の渦
findings.governingReading: a vortex of light that burns away whatever it touches
findings.explanation: The English omits the vortex form of the attack that stops Shirou’s projection.

findings.governingReading: Gilgamesh’s sword, read specifically as Gram
findings.explanation: The English drops the Gram ruby and therefore the weapon identity Shirou associates with the repelled attack.

findings.evidenceJa: 尻餅をついた状態で、セイバーに背中を支えられながら
findings.governingReading: Seated heavily on the ground, Shirou looks down while Saber supports his back.
findings.explanation: The English omits both his seated fall and the exact support at his back, weakening spatial continuity into the later embrace.

findings.evidenceJa: それは、どのくらいの強さだったのか
findings.governingReading: How strong was that embrace or pressure?
findings.explanation: The English turns Shirou’s fading perception of the embrace’s strength into a general question about Saber’s power.
